messages:
Alex: morning — pushed a tiny header-parsing hotfix to api-gateway, rolled to staging. deploy-bot reported success.
Maria: nice, any fallout?
Alex: none so far, but noticed auth latency spikes during cold-starts (200ms -> ~1.2s) on the introspect path.
Kevin: is that token introspect? I changed a cache TTL yesterday, could be expiries aligning.
Tanya: blocker: my laptop can't run the e2e suite — docker credential error. I need infra help to regen creds.
Alex: @infra oncall can you help Tanya with docker creds? :pray:
deploy-bot: deploy alex/gateway-hotfix -> staging succeeded (1836012380)
Sam: what I did: added a route predicate for X-Client-Version and unit tests. PR #3421 is awaiting review.
Maria: I'll take a look after standup, pinging now.
Kevin: quick Q: should rate-limits be enforced before auth or after? current edge policy applies a global limiter.
Tanya: my vote: run auth first so we can enforce per-user quotas, but keep a cheap global throttle at the edge to protect the backend.
Alex: agreed — auth-first for per-user quotas, plus a cheap global limiter (token-bucket) at ~1000 rps.
Maria: also we need metrics to distinguish drops due to auth failures vs rate-limit hits. Add counters and tags.
Sam: adding a TODO in the policy config, example snippet: 
```yaml
policies:
  - name: cheap-global-throttle
    type: token_bucket
    rate: 1000
  - name: auth-and-user-quotas
    type: auth_then_quota
```
Kevin: also request: can we land the routing policy change today? it touches canary rules — propose a 5% canary.
Alex: plan: merge tomorrow AM, canary 5% for 2h, monitor errors/latency, rollback if anomalies.
Tanya: blocker cleared: infra-sig rotated my creds, I can run e2e now and will smoke-test the auth flow.
Maria: anything else?
Alex: fyi I created a small eval prompt set for auth-regressions to catch token edge-cases; linked in the PR description.
Sam: I'll add a unit that asserts X-Client-Version routing behavior too.
Kevin: thanks all :thumbsup:
Maria: end of check-in.
